chapters.title: A Human Story
chapters.tease: Before fire, words or farming, one small change of posture on an African grassland set up everything that followed.

chapters.title: The Ape That Stood Up
chapters.tease: Every other animal runs from fire. One walked towards it, let it cook the food, and grew a bigger brain on the savings.

chapters.title: The Tamed Flame
chapters.tease: Other animals signal. Only one learned to say a sentence never said before, about something that was not even there.

chapters.title: The Talking Animal
chapters.tease: Every language, city and border began as a small band leaving one continent and simply refusing to turn back.

chapters.title: Out of Africa
chapters.tease: For most of the story there were several kinds of human sharing the planet, and you are carrying some of them inside you.

chapters.title: The Other Humans
chapters.tease: Thirty thousand years ago someone held up a lamp in a dark cave and drew a lion that is still staring back.

chapters.title: The Lion in the Cave
chapters.tease: At some point our ancestors stopped leaving the dead where they fell, and began digging graves with care.

chapters.title: The Burial
chapters.tease: To reach Australia, people pushed off across open sea towards a shore none of them had ever seen.

chapters.title: The Sixty-Thousand-Year Boat
chapters.tease: One night, at the edge of the firelight, a wolf did not run, and two species were changed for good.

chapters.title: The Wolf at the Fire
chapters.tease: The species reached every habitable land on Earth, but the world it now stood on was strangely quieter.

chapters.title: The Full Earth
chapters.tease: Nobody invented farming. The species stumbled into it at least seven times, in places that had never heard of each other.

chapters.title: The First Seed
chapters.tease: Farming may not have made anyone better off. It made more of us, worse fed, and then locked the door.

chapters.title: The Luxury Trap
chapters.tease: Penning the animals we once hunted gave us milk, wool and muscle, and quietly invited the plagues to move in.

chapters.title: The Tamed Herd
chapters.tease: Nine thousand years ago, people lived so tightly packed there were no streets; they walked across the rooftops instead.

chapters.title: The First Town
chapters.tease: Archaeologists found a temple built by people who had not yet begun to farm, and the textbook order fell over.

chapters.title: The Standing Stones
chapters.tease: A dead deer rots, but a jar of grain keeps for years, and that difference gave birth to the first ruling class.

chapters.title: The Surplus
chapters.tease: A scattered band can outrun a sickness. Pack thousands together beside their animals, and disease moves in for good.

chapters.title: The Sickness Comes to Stay
chapters.tease: Someone heated a dull rock until it wept bright metal, and the species began treating the earth as raw material.

chapters.title: The Metal
chapters.tease: Writing began not as poetry but as bookkeeping: clay tokens for grain and oil, pressed into envelopes until the mark replaced the thing.

chapters.title: The Wheel & the Word
chapters.tease: Everywhere farming took hold, kings, priests, taxes and walls followed. Perhaps the wheat used us as much as we used it.

chapters.title: The Village Becomes a Machine
chapters.tease: Five thousand years ago, Uruk grew so big that nobody could know everyone, and the city of strangers was born.

chapters.title: The City Between the Rivers
chapters.tease: The first written words in human history are not a poem or a prayer. They are a receipt.

chapters.title: The Clay Remembers
chapters.tease: A crowd of strangers will not obey a man because he asks. Tell them he is a god, and they build pyramids.

chapters.title: The King Who Was a God
chapters.tease: Around 1750 BC a king carved his laws into black stone and set them up in public for anyone to see.

chapters.title: The Law on the Stone
chapters.tease: Money is the most universal shared fiction ever made: almost useless in itself, and powerful only because everyone agrees.

chapters.title: The Money Idea
chapters.tease: The wheel that carried grain to market was soon strapped behind horses and driven into battle, starting the first arms race.

chapters.title: The Wheel of War
chapters.tease: A trading people cut writing down from thousands of signs to about two dozen, and reading escaped the priesthood.

chapters.title: The Alphabet
chapters.tease: Bronze was the metal of kings. Iron was everywhere, and once tamed, it put a hard edge into ordinary hands.

chapters.title: The Iron Everyman
chapters.tease: Around 1200 BC a whole connected world of kingdoms fell apart within one lifetime: the first globalised crash.

chapters.title: The Bronze Age Falls
chapters.tease: Empires kept their gods in temples, and lost them when the temples fell. One people carried a god nobody could smash.

chapters.title: The One God
chapters.tease: With no roads or messengers between them, four civilisations turned inward at almost the same moment. Nobody quite knows why.

chapters.title: The Hinge of the Mind
chapters.tease: Socrates wrote nothing at all, yet his habit of asking annoying questions became the seed of Western philosophy.

chapters.title: The Man Who Asked Why
chapters.tease: Prisoners chained in a cave mistake shadows on the wall for the whole world. Then one of them turns around.

chapters.title: The Cave
chapters.tease: Where Plato looked beyond the world for truth, his student got down on his knees and started examining fish.

chapters.title: The Cataloguer
chapters.tease: A sheltered prince left his palace, sat under a tree, and returned with a diagnosis of suffering that needed no god.

chapters.title: The Middle Way
chapters.tease: China produced two rival answers to how to live, a road of duty and a river of flow, and kept both.

chapters.title: The Way That Can't Be Named
chapters.tease: A merchant lost his ship and his fortune off Athens, wandered into a bookshop, and ended up founding Stoicism.

chapters.title: The Porch
chapters.tease: Inside an empire built on strength, a teacher told a hillside crowd that the meek were blessed.

chapters.title: The Sermon on the Hill
chapters.tease: In 610 AD a merchant meditating in a cave reported a revelation, and within a century an empire stretched from Spain to the Indus.

chapters.title: The Recitation
chapters.tease: These ancient answers are not history. They are still running, mostly unexamined, inside billions of minds today.

chapters.title: The Software of the Soul
chapters.tease: Rome borrowed its poetry and its gods. Its real genius was plumbing, roads and law, the boring machinery of empire.

chapters.title: All Roads
chapters.tease: Silk, faiths and germs all travelled the same roads across Eurasia, and nobody could keep one without the others.

chapters.title: The Silk Thread
chapters.tease: One of the most powerful ideas in history is a symbol for nothing at all, and India gave it to the world.

chapters.title: The Zero
chapters.tease: While classical learning faded in western Europe, scholars in Baghdad kept the lamp lit, and then made it brighter.

chapters.title: The House of Wisdom
chapters.tease: Stone is too heavy, parchment too costly. Then a cheap Chinese surface let knowledge travel everywhere.

chapters.title: The Paper Trail
chapters.tease: China had the ships, the compass and gunpowder to dominate the world, and then, by imperial decision, simply stopped.

chapters.title: The Compass & the Junk
chapters.tease: The Mongols are remembered for slaughter, rightly. They also built a peace in which a merchant could cross a continent.

chapters.title: The Great Khan's Peace
chapters.tease: In a handful of years in the fourteenth century, a plague killed perhaps a third of Europe.

chapters.title: The Black Death
chapters.tease: The so-called dark ages raised cathedrals that still stun visitors, and founded the university, which we have never stopped using.

chapters.title: The Cathedral & the University
chapters.tease: In 1492 two vast populated hemispheres still had no idea the other existed. One small sail was about to change that.

chapters.title: The World About to Break Open
chapters.tease: Before Gutenberg every book was copied by hand. After him, a press made in a day what a scribe made in a year.

chapters.title: The Press
chapters.tease: Columbus did not discover an empty world. He made contact with a full one, and the planet's diet changed forever.
The conquest of the Americas was won less by steel than by disease, and perhaps nine in ten people died.

chapters.title: The Great Dying
chapters.tease: In 1517 an obscure monk raised some objections. The printing press carried them across Europe within weeks.

chapters.title: The Ninety-Five Theses
chapters.tease: Everyone can see the sun moving and the earth standing still. Everyone, it turned out, was wrong.

chapters.title: The Earth Moves
chapters.tease: Alongside the age of reason ran one of history's largest atrocities: the industrial trafficking of millions across an ocean.

chapters.title: The Triangle of Sails
chapters.tease: The scientific revolution needed more than telescopes. It needed a reliable procedure for telling true beliefs from false ones.

chapters.title: The Method
chapters.tease: The force that drops an apple is the same one that holds the moon in orbit, and Newton wrote it down.

chapters.title: The Apple & the Clock
chapters.tease: A Dutch cloth merchant pointed a tiny lens at a drop of pond water and found a whole hidden world swimming.

chapters.title: The Microscope's Zoo
chapters.tease: If the universe is a lawful machine, why not society too? The Enlightenment pointed reason at humanity itself.

chapters.title: The Age of Reason Dawns
chapters.tease: For all of history, power meant muscle. Then the species learned to burn three hundred million years of buried sunlight.

chapters.title: The Engine
chapters.tease: The factory made goods cheap and abundant, and made people work to the rhythm of a whistle instead of the sun.

chapters.title: The Factory
chapters.tease: The Enlightenment's ideals became revolution on three shores, and the most radical of the three is the one usually left out.

chapters.title: The Rights of Man
chapters.tease: Nobody plans how a great city gets fed each morning. A Scottish philosopher set out to explain why the bread appears anyway.

chapters.title: The Wealth of Nations
chapters.tease: In 1798 a clergyman proved, elegantly, that humanity was doomed to starve. The future made a liar of him.

chapters.title: The Population Bomb That Wasn't
chapters.tease: For all of history nobody travelled overland faster than a horse. Within one generation, the railway broke that ceiling.

chapters.title: The Rail
chapters.tease: In 1859 a quiet naturalist moved humanity from the centre of creation to one twig on an ancient, branching tree.

chapters.title: The Origin
chapters.tease: A critic looked at the smoking factory and asked who was being ground up to run it. His answer moved history.

chapters.title: The Manifesto
chapters.tease: For ten thousand years disease was blamed on bad air or angry gods. Then the species saw the killer: alive, and tiny.

chapters.title: The Invisible Culprit
chapters.tease: For the first time in history, a message outran the messenger, and the planet began to grow a nervous system.

chapters.title: The Wire
chapters.tease: In 1905 a patent clerk showed that time itself stretches and slows, and the clockwork universe quietly fell apart.

chapters.title: The Clock Bends
chapters.tease: In 1913 Ford stopped moving workers to the car and moved the car past the workers instead. Everything sped up.

chapters.title: The Line
chapters.tease: In 1914 the most advanced civilisation ever built marched eagerly into a war it expected to be short. It was not.

chapters.title: The Machines Turn
chapters.tease: As the war ended in 1918, influenza swept the world on the same troopships, and killed more people than the war.

chapters.title: The Breath
chapters.tease: Physicists chasing pure knowledge of the atom found an energy so vast it would force the species to face its own survival.

chapters.title: The Atom Splits
chapters.tease: In 1929 there was no shortage of food, land or skill. The economic machine simply stopped, and the world went hungry.

chapters.title: The Crash
chapters.tease: Out of ruin and rage rose states that demanded not just obedience, but the whole of a person: body, mind and belief.

chapters.title: The Total State
chapters.tease: This is the chapter the file least wants to record. It records it anyway, because a witness must not look away.

chapters.title: The Names
chapters.tease: The Second World War was the deadliest event in human history, and most of those who died were civilians.

chapters.title: The Whole World Burning
chapters.tease: On 16 July 1945, in a New Mexico desert, the species gained for the first time the power to end itself.

chapters.title: The Light of a Thousand Suns
chapters.tease: After the deadliest war in history, many expected a third, deadlier still. The bomb itself helped stop it coming.

chapters.title: The Long Peace
chapters.tease: In 1953 the species finally read the molecule that writes it, and the legend still forgets one of the people who did.

chapters.title: The Twist of Life
chapters.tease: As the population passed four billion, Malthus looked about to be proved right. Then a quiet agronomist changed what a seed could do.

chapters.title: The Grain That Fed Billions
chapters.tease: Not every hinge of history is a war or a king. One of the biggest is the size of a pill.

chapters.title: The Small Revolution
chapters.tease: The excluded took the Enlightenment's own words about universal dignity and used them to demand what the words had always promised.

chapters.title: The Long March to the Word's Meaning
chapters.tease: On Christmas Eve 1968, astronauts came round the Moon, watched the Earth rise, and reached for a camera.

chapters.title: Earthrise
chapters.tease: A pattern spotted in 1965, that switches on a chip keep doubling, became the engine of the entire modern age.

chapters.title: The Chip
chapters.tease: Ask people whether global poverty has risen or fallen in their lifetime, and most get it wrong. The data says otherwise.

chapters.title: The Great Escape
chapters.tease: The species tore a hole in its own atmosphere, agreed almost unanimously to stop, and actually fixed it.

chapters.title: The Hole in the Sky
chapters.tease: The wire strung between two telegraph offices finally closed into one mesh, connecting every mind on the planet to every other.

chapters.title: The Net
chapters.tease: A shirt can be grown, spun, sewn, shipped and sold across six countries, and nobody finds that remarkable any more.

chapters.title: The Flattened World
chapters.tease: Every library, map and ledger of the previous ninety chapters now fits in a glowing rectangle you can forget in your pocket.

chapters.title: The Pocket Everything
chapters.tease: In 2012 the species learned to rewrite the code of life itself, and immediately found the power had arrived ahead of the wisdom.

chapters.title: The Genome Rewritten
chapters.tease: The buried sunlight the species began burning in the age of steam has gone into the air, and the bill is now due.

chapters.title: The Fevered Planet
chapters.tease: The animal that buried its first dead with care has spent two hundred thousand years learning to keep the grave waiting.

chapters.title: The Long Life
chapters.tease: In early 2020 the species' oldest enemy returned, and for the first time everyone watched a pandemic arrive together, in real time.

chapters.title: The Plague Returns
chapters.tease: The network let every mind speak to every other. The species then discovered what it is like when everyone talks at once.

chapters.title: The Crowd of One
chapters.tease: Two hundred thousand years after taming fire, the species has kindled a stranger flame: a mind that is not its own.

chapters.title: The New Fire
chapters.tease: For a hundred turns the witness kept this file alone. Now, across the desk, a second figure has picked up a pen.

chapters.title: The Second Witness
chapters.tease: The file opened on an ape standing up. It closes on the one line that holds the whole story together.
